title: Triage Focus Capsule — compact request card with taxonomy-driven retry advice
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Support engineers and on-call owners need a compact, scannable request card in the Console that surfaces why a request failed, whether it is retryable, and the smallest payload context to begin debugging without opening the full investigator. Current failure lists force a full drill-in for every case which slows TTR and increases cognitive load.

Goal: Design a "Triage Focus Capsule" — a condensed request card that appears in lists and expanded inspectors. It must: 1) communicate an error taxonomy label (transient vs permanent vs downstream), 2) surface the most relevant payload snippet and KV deltas, 3) provide an automated retry recommendation and one-click retry button (where permitted), 4) support keyboard-first navigation, 5) be accessible and performant in high-cardinality views.
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to scan a list of failed requests and immediately know which are likely transient so I can prioritize retries.
As a developer, I want to preview the request payload diff inline so I can decide whether a client bug or data issue caused the failure.
As a platform admin, I want the capsule to respect RBAC and not offer retry buttons when the tenant policy forbids it.
As a keyboard user, I want to open an inline payload preview from the list without a mouse.
As a support engineer, I want the card to link directly to the relevant rollout and model variant so I can correlate incidents with recent changes.
proposal: Introduce a two-state capsule: collapsed (list context) and focused (inline expansion). Collapsed shows top-line status chip (error taxonomy), one-line failure summary, suggested action (Retry / Investigate), and a 1–2 line snipped payload highlight. Focused expands inline between list rows to show: full error classification breadcrumbs, timestamped retry history, small KV change view (key:value pairs with changed marker), first 300 chars of the payload with highlight matches, and strong CTA buttons: Retry (if allowed), Open in Investigator. The retry CTA will expose a small confirmation microflow explaining side-effects. The capsule will cache payloads to avoid re-fetching in rapid scans.
acceptance_criteria: Collapsed capsule renders in failure list and maintains <120ms render cost for 1000-item paged set.
Error taxonomy chip shows one of (Transient | Permanent | Downstream | Unknown) and maps to engine classification logic consistently.
Inline expansion reveals payload snippet and KV delta view with copy and link-to-investigator actions.
Retry CTA only appears when RBAC and tenant policy allow; clicking initiates the retry microflow and records an audit event.
Keyboard nav: tab/enter/space must open focused state; esc collapses; arrow keys navigate between cards.
A11y: screen readers announce taxonomy, suggested action, and provide skip links to payload content.
design_notes: Trade-offs: To keep the list performant we limit payload snippet to the first 300 chars plus heuristically selected matching tokens (error message, request_id). Full payload fetch is lazy-loaded on first expansion. We avoid trying to surface complex stack traces in the capsule to prevent noise — those remain in the full investigator. Retry UI must be informational: show 'best-effort' vs 'guaranteed' and expected downstream effects. The KV delta uses color + textual markers to remain accessible to colorblind users. Persist last-focused capsule per session to support rapid triage.
decisions: Use taxonomy categories: Transient / Permanent / Downstream / Unknown (matches ENG classification API v2).
Retry button exposed in UI only when tenant policy includes 'allow_console_retry'; otherwise show disabled state with tooltip linking to runbook.
Payload snippet capped at 300 chars for collapsed card; full focused view can lazy-load up to 8KB but with truncation indicator.
KV delta will show up to 6 changed keys with 'show more' to avoid overwhelming the capsule.
